cards.text: Pilate, the Roman governor, has handed Jesus over to be crucified, and the soldiers have taken Him away (John 19:16). Friend, this one is heavy, so stay close to me. Carrying His own cross, Jesus goes out to a place with a grim name.

cards.question: Carrying His own cross, Jesus goes out to The Place of the ___, which in Hebrew is called Golgotha.

cards.text: There they crucify Him. And He is not the only one crucified there.

cards.question: Two others are crucified with Jesus, one on each side, with Jesus in the middle.

cards.text: Pilate isn't done yet. He has a notice posted right on the cross.

cards.question: Pilate's notice on the cross names Jesus of Nazareth. What does it call Him?

cards.text: Many of the Jews read this sign, because the place where Jesus was crucified is near the city.

cards.question: Pilate's notice on the cross is written in Hebrew, Latin and Greek.

cards.text: The chief priests read it too, and they go to Pilate. They want the wording changed on a sign that's already up on a cross.

cards.question: The chief priests don't want Pilate's sign to say “The King of the Jews.” What do they want it to say instead?

answers.text: That He said He was King of the Jews
That He was a criminal from Nazareth
That He was a false teacher from Galilee

cards.question: Pilate gives in to the chief priests and changes the sign on the cross.

cards.text: Pilate answers, “What I have written, I have written.” Friend, that's not a reply. That's a door closing.
When the soldiers have crucified Jesus, they divide His garments into four parts, one for each soldier. But His tunic is left over.

cards.question: Jesus' tunic is seamless, woven in one piece from top to bottom. What do the soldiers decide to do with it?

answers.text: Cast lots to see who gets it
Tear it into four even pieces
Leave it at the foot of the cross

cards.question: John says the soldiers casting lots for Jesus' tunic happens to fulfill the ___.

cards.text: John points to the Scripture: “They divided My garments among them, and cast lots for My clothing.” (Psalm 22:18) And that is what the soldiers did.
Not everyone has walked away. Near the cross stand Mary the wife of Clopas, and Mary Magdalene, one of the women who traveled with Jesus (Luke 8:1-2).

cards.question: Jesus' mother and her sister are also standing near the cross.

cards.text: Jesus sees His mother. And standing nearby is someone John only calls “the disciple whom He loved.”

cards.question: From the cross, Jesus speaks to His mother about the disciple whom He loved. What does He say?

answers.text: Woman do not weep for Me

cards.question: Then Jesus turns to the disciple whom He loved and says, “Here is your ___.”
From that hour, the disciple whom Jesus loved takes Jesus' mother into his home.

cards.text: After this, Jesus knows that everything has now been accomplished. And to fulfill the Scripture, He says, “I am thirsty.”
A jar of sour wine is sitting there.

cards.question: Jesus is on the cross, and a jar of sour wine is sitting there. How do they lift the wine to His mouth?

answers.text: On a sponge on a stalk of hyssop
In a cup on the tip of a spear
In a jar raised up on a ladder

cards.text: Jesus receives the sour wine. Then He speaks one more time.

cards.question: Jesus knows that everything has now been accomplished. What does He say after He receives the sour wine?

cards.text: And bowing His head, He yields up His spirit. Sit with that one a minute, friend, because this story is not over.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 10 quotes "The King of the Jews.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: Stop 2, card 3 quotes "the disciple whom He loved.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: Card 1 says Jesus goes to 'a place with a grim name.' That hint rules out 'Palms,' and mostly 'Stones,' so 'Skull' is the only grim choice left.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: This card asks for a place name. Its wrong answers, 'The Place of the Stones' and 'The Place of the Palms,' are not real places from the Bible.

rule.text: For who, which thing and where questions, wrong answers are real details from somewhere in the Bible, like Joppa when the right answer is Tarshish.

findings.problem: The question types in stop 1 alternate strictly from card 4 to card 14: true or false, multiple choice, true or false, multiple choice, true or false, multiple choice. Stop 2 starts with the same true or false, multiple choice pairing.

rule.text: Which question type comes next, the order the types come in and where a blank falls are chosen naturally for each card. They never follow a pattern. No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: The card says the casting of lots 'happens to fulfill' the Scripture. That makes it sound like a coincidence. John 19:24 says 'This was to fulfill the Scripture,' which states a purpose.

rule.text: Retelling: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: 'Not everyone has walked away' says that other people walked away. John 19:25 doesn't say that, and nothing else in the passage does either. The storyteller line adds a fact.

rule.text: Papa Dorin can add a storyteller's line to carry the moment, like "But the Lord isn't finished with him," as long as it adds no facts.

findings.problem: The question says Jesus speaks to His mother 'about the disciple whom He loved.' Only the right answer, 'Woman here is your son,' is about the disciple. The other two answers are ruled out by the question itself.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The question begins 'Jesus knows that everything has now been accomplished.' That matches 'It is finished' and rules out 'It has only begun,' so the choice is close to a giveaway.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.
